source.text: וְדָוִ֥יד זָקֵ֖ן וְשָׂבַ֣ע יָמִ֑ים וַיַּמְלֵ֛ךְ אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And David [was] old and full of days, and he made king Solomon his son over Israel.

en.L: And David was old and full of days, and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
en.B: When David was old and had lived a full life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
en.R: David was now old and had lived a long, full life. He made his son Solomon king over Israel.

decisions.choice: full of days: having lived a long and complete life
decisions.reason: To be "full of days" is to have had all the years of life one could wish for, said of Isaac (Genesis 35:29) and Job (Job 42:17). It is a mark of blessing, not of weakness.

decisions.choice: a short summary of Solomon's accession
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 1 tells at length how Solomon came to the throne while David was "old, advanced in days" (1 Kings 1:1), against the claim of his brother Adonijah. Chronicles gives only the bare fact here, as a heading for David's last arrangements in chapters 23-29, and tells of Solomon being made king again before all the assembly in 29:22.

decisions.choice: had lived a full life / had lived a long, full life
decisions.reason: As in Genesis 35:29, Balanced and Readable say what "full of days" means; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

source.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹף֙ אֶת־כָּל־שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gathered all [the] princes of Israel and the priests and the Levites.

en.L: And he gathered all the princes of Israel and the priests and the Levites.
en.B: He gathered together all the officials of Israel, and the priests and the Levites.
en.R: He called together all the leaders of Israel, and the priests and the Levites.

decisions.choice: the gathering at which the arrangements of chapters 23-27 are made
decisions.reason: This assembly is the setting for the lists of Levites, priests, singers, gatekeepers and officials that follow. David speaks to the gathered leaders again in 28:1.

decisions.choice: princes: the leading men of the tribes and the royal court
decisions.reason: The word names men of rank and authority: tribal leaders, heads of clans and royal officials (27:22; 28:1).

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders
decisions.reason: The usual wording for this word in these books: "princes" at Literal, "officials" at Balanced, "leaders" at Readable.

source.text: וַיִּסָּֽפְרוּ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיְהִ֨י מִסְפָּרָ֤ם לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָם֙ לִגְבָרִ֔ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁמוֹנָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And were counted the Levites from [a] son of thirty year[s] and upward, and was their number by their skulls, of men, thirty and eight thousand.

en.L: And the Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward, and their number by their heads, man by man, was 38,000.
en.B: The Levites who were thirty years old and over were counted, and the total, counted man by man, was 38,000.
en.R: The Levites who were thirty years old or older were counted. There were 38,000 men.

decisions.choice: thirty years old and upward: the working age set by the law of Moses
decisions.reason: Numbers 4:3 counts the Levites who carried the tabernacle from thirty years old. Verses 24 and 27 of this chapter give twenty as the age; see the note at verse 24.

decisions.choice: by their skulls, of men: a head count of the men
decisions.reason: "By their skulls" means counting one person at a time, as in the census of Numbers 1:2. Only men were counted for this service.

decisions.choice: thousand: read as the number
decisions.reason: On the word "thousand" and the size of such totals, see the note at the census in Numbers 1:21: the word can also name a clan or military unit.

decisions.choice: counted man by man / There were 38,000 men
decisions.reason: Balanced folds "by their skulls" into "counted man by man"; Readable gives just the number of men.

source.text: מֵאֵ֗לֶּה לְנַצֵּ֨חַ֙ עַל־מְלֶ֣אכֶת בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וְשֹׁטְרִ֥ים וְשֹׁפְטִ֖ים שֵׁ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: From these [are] to oversee the work of [the] house of Yahweh twenty and four thousand, and officers and judges six thousand,

en.L: "Of these, 24,000 [are] to oversee the work of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and 6,000 [are to be] officials and judges,
en.B: David said, "Of these, 24,000 are to direct the work on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and 6,000 are to serve as officials and judges,
en.R: David said, "Of these men, 24,000 will be in charge of the work at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. Another 6,000 will be officials and judges.

decisions.choice: David's own words, though no speech is announced
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves straight from the count to the plan, with no "David said". The "I made" of verse 5 shows that verses 4-5 are David's words.

decisions.choice: to oversee: to direct and lead the work
decisions.reason: The verb means to supervise or lead, used of the overseers of the temple's building and repair (Ezra 3:8-9; 2 Chronicles 34:12). The same root appears in the heading "for the director" of many psalms.

decisions.choice: officials and judges: men who kept records, carried out orders and settled cases
decisions.reason: These are the two offices of Deuteronomy 16:18. Their work was away from the house of God, among the people (26:29 names Levites for this "outside work").

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the temple still to be built
decisions.reason: David is preparing for the temple Solomon will build (22:1-19). The plan looks ahead to its work.

decisions.choice: David said,
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is speaking, since the Hebrew's switch to David's own words in verse 5 would otherwise come as a surprise. Literal opens the quotation without supplied words.

decisions.choice: the LORD's temple
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD" throughout, since the building, not a home, is meant.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The same word is "officials" at Deuteronomy 16:18 and Joshua 1:10, and at 26:29 and 27:1 in this book.

source.text: וְאַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים שֹׁעֲרִ֑ים וְאַרְבַּ֤עַת אֲלָפִים֙ מְהַֽלְלִ֣ים לַיהוָ֔ה בַּכֵּלִ֕ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי לְהַלֵּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: and four thousand gatekeepers, and four thousand praising Yahweh with the instruments which I made for praising.

en.L: and 4,000 gatekeepers, and 4,000 praising {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with the instruments that I made for praising."
en.B: 4,000 are to be gatekeepers, while 4,000 are to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, playing the instruments I made for giving praise."
en.R: Another 4,000 will be gatekeepers, and another 4,000 will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with the musical instruments I have made for praise."

decisions.choice: I made: David speaks of the instruments he had made
decisions.reason: The first person shows that David is speaking. The ancient Greek translation has "which he made", which turns the verse back into the narrator's report; the Hebrew text is kept. David is remembered as a maker of instruments (2 Chronicles 7:6; 29:26-27; Amos 6:5).

decisions.choice: gatekeepers: guards of the gates and storerooms of the house of God
decisions.reason: Their divisions are listed in 26:1-19, and their duties are described in 9:17-27.

decisions.choice: praising with instruments: the singers and musicians
decisions.reason: Their divisions are listed in chapter 25. They played cymbals, harps and lyres (15:16; 25:1).

decisions.choice: musical instruments
decisions.reason: Readable adds "musical", since the word can mean any tool or vessel.

source.text: וַיֶּֽחָלְקֵ֥ם דָּוִ֖יד מַחְלְק֑וֹתסלִבְנֵ֣י לֵוִ֔י לְגֵרְשׁ֖וֹן קְהָ֥ת וּמְרָרִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And divided them David [into] divisions by [the] sons of Levi: to Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

en.L: And David divided them [into] divisions by the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
en.B: David organized them into divisions by the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
en.R: David divided the Levites into groups by the families of Levi's three sons: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

decisions.choice: divisions: groups that took turns on duty
decisions.reason: The word means a portion or share. In chapters 23-27 it names the groups of Levites, priests, singers, gatekeepers and soldiers who served in turn (24:1; 26:1; 27:1).

decisions.choice: Gershon, Kohath and Merari: the three sons of Levi
decisions.reason: The same three are named in Exodus 6:16, Numbers 3:17 and 1 Chronicles 5:27. In 6:1-2 the first is spelled Gershom; here, as in Exodus and Numbers, he is Gershon.

decisions.choice: the families of Levi's three sons
decisions.reason: Readable says that the divisions follow the families descended from Levi's sons.

source.text: לַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י לַעְדָּ֥ן וְשִׁמְעִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: To the Gershonite[s]: Ladan and Shimei.

en.L: Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
en.B: The Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
en.R: From the family of Gershon came Ladan and Shimei.

decisions.choice: Ladan: probably the same family as Libni
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the sons of Gershon are Libni and Shimei (Exodus 6:17; Numbers 3:18; 1 Chronicles 6:2). Ladan is named only in Chronicles (here and 26:21). He may be Libni under another name, or a later head of that family.

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י לַעְדָּ֗ן הָרֹ֧אשׁ יְחִיאֵ֛ל וְזֵתָ֥ם וְיוֹאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Ladan: the head Jehiel, and Zetham and Joel, three.

en.L: The sons of Ladan: the head, Jehiel, and Zetham and Joel, three.
en.B: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham and Joel, three in all.
en.R: Ladan's sons were Jehiel the leader, Zetham and Joel. That was three.

decisions.choice: the head: the leading member of the family line
decisions.reason: The word "head" marks the man who led his branch of the family, perhaps the eldest. It recurs through the chapter (verses 11, 16-20).

decisions.choice: three: the count closes each family list
decisions.reason: The totals at the end of verses 8-12 and 23 help the reader check each list, as in the census lists of Numbers.

decisions.choice: the head / the chief / the leader
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "head". Balanced says "chief" and Readable "leader"; where "the second" follows, both say "the first" (verses 11, 19, 20).

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְעִ֗י שְׁלוֹמִ֧ית וַחֲזִיאֵ֛ל וְהָרָ֖ן שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה אֵ֛לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י הָאָב֖וֹת לְלַעְדָּֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Shimei: Shelomoth and Haziel and Haran, three. These [were the] heads of the fathers of Ladan.

en.L: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth and Haziel and Haran, three. These [were] the heads of the fathers' [houses] of Ladan.
en.B: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel and Haran, three in all. These were the heads of the families of Ladan.
en.R: Shimei's sons were Shelomoth, Haziel and Haran. That was three. These were the leaders of Ladan's family groups.

decisions.choice: Shelomoth, as the reading in the margin has it
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has Shelomith, and the reading handed down in the margin has Shelomoth. The margin's form is kept here. A Levite of verse 18 is also called Shelomith, and appears as Shelomoth in 24:22.

decisions.choice: Shimei here: probably a son of Ladan, not the brother of verse 7
alternatives: the same Shimei as in verses 7 and 10
decisions.reason: These three are called heads of Ladan's families, so this Shimei seems to be a son of Ladan, otherwise unnamed. The Shimei of verse 7, Ladan's brother, has his own sons in verse 10. The text may also have suffered in copying, with another of Ladan's sons first written here.

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers' [houses] / heads of the families
decisions.reason: As in 9:33-34, Literal shows the Hebrew "heads of the fathers" with brackets, and Balanced and Readable speak of families.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְעִ֔י יַ֣חַת זִינָ֔א וִיע֖וּשׁ וּבְרִיעָ֑ה אֵ֥לֶּה בְנֵי־שִׁמְעִ֖י אַרְבָּעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, and Jeush and Beriah. These [were the] sons of Shimei, four.

en.L: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, and Jeush and Beriah. These [were] the sons of Shimei, four.
en.B: The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei, four in all.
en.R: Shimei's sons were Jahath, Zina, Jeush and Beriah. These four were Shimei's sons.

decisions.choice: Zina: the same man as Zizah in verse 11
decisions.reason: The next verse calls him Zizah, and some ancient translations read Zizah here too. The two forms differ by one letter that is easily confused in Hebrew writing. The text is kept as it stands.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי־יַ֣חַת הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְזִיזָ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וִיע֤וּשׁ וּבְרִיעָה֙ לֹֽא־הִרְבּ֣וּ בָנִ֔ים וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ לְבֵ֣ית אָ֔ב לִפְקֻדָּ֖ה אֶחָֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And was Jahath the head, and Zizah the second; and Jeush and Beriah did not make many sons, and they became for a house of a father, for one enrollment.

en.L: And Jahath was the head, and Zizah the second; and Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, and they became one father's house, for one enrollment.
en.B: Jahath was the first and Zizah the second. Jeush and Beriah had few sons, so they were counted as a single family with one assignment.
en.R: Jahath was the first, and Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons. So their families were counted together as one family group with one duty.

decisions.choice: one enrollment: a single unit for duty
decisions.reason: The word means a counting, or the post a counted group was given. Two small families were counted together as one father's house, so that they took one turn of service together.

decisions.choice: the head ... the second: an order of rank
decisions.reason: "The head" here stands first in a numbered list, and so means the first. Verses 19 and 20 follow the same pattern.

decisions.choice: the first
decisions.reason: Where "the second" follows, Balanced and Readable say "the first" for "the head", as verse 8's decision says.

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י קְהָ֗ת עַמְרָ֥ם יִצְהָ֛ר חֶבְר֥וֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, four.

en.L: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, four.
en.B: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, four in all.
en.R: Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. That was four.

decisions.choice: the four sons of Kohath
decisions.reason: The same four are named in Exodus 6:18, Numbers 3:19 and 1 Chronicles 5:28.

source.text: בְּנֵ֥י עַמְרָ֖ם אַהֲרֹ֣ן וּמֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבָּדֵ֣ל אַהֲרֹ֡ן לְֽהַקְדִּישׁוֹ֩ קֹ֨דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֤ים הֽוּא־וּבָנָיו֙ עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם לְהַקְטִיר֩ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה לְשָׁרְת֛וֹ וּלְבָרֵ֥ךְ בִּשְׁמ֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And was set apart Aaron to consecrate it, holy of holies, he and his sons until forever, to make smoke before Yahweh, to serve him and to bless in his name until forever.

en.L: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn [offerings] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to minister to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to bless in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name forever.
en.B: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart, he and his sons for all time, to consecrate the most holy things, to burn offerings before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to minister to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to bless in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name forever.
en.R: Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen and set apart forever to make the most holy things holy. They were to burn offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And they were to bless the people in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name for all time.

decisions.choice: to consecrate the most holy things
alternatives: to be consecrated as most holy
decisions.reason: The verb has an ending "it" or "him". Read as "it", Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things, the holiest offerings and objects of the sanctuary (Exodus 30:29; Numbers 18:9-10). Read as "him", the sense is that Aaron was set apart to be consecrated as most holy. The first reading fits the list of tasks that follows.

decisions.choice: to burn offerings: to make offerings go up in smoke on the altar
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something smoke. It is used both of burning incense (Exodus 30:7) and of burning the parts of a sacrifice on the altar (Leviticus 1:9). Both were the work of the priests alone (2 Chronicles 26:18).

decisions.choice: to bless in his name: the priestly blessing
decisions.reason: The words echo Deuteronomy 10:8 and 21:5, and the blessing that Aaron and his sons were to speak over Israel in the LORD's name (Numbers 6:23-27).

decisions.choice: set apart, he and his sons forever: the priesthood belongs to Aaron's line
decisions.reason: The verse marks the line between the priests and the other Levites: Moses' sons are counted among the Levites (verse 14), while Aaron's line alone serves as priests (Numbers 18:1-7).

decisions.choice: bless the people
decisions.reason: Readable says who is blessed, as in Deuteronomy 10:8, and uses "descendants" for "sons" since the line runs on for all time.

source.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּנָ֕יו יִקָּרְא֖וּ עַל־שֵׁ֥בֶט הַלֵּוִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And Moses, [the] man of God, his sons were named among [the] tribe of the Levite[s].

en.L: And Moses the man of God: his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
en.B: As for Moses the man of God, his sons were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
en.R: Moses was a man of God, but his sons were counted only as members of the tribe of Levi.

decisions.choice: man of God: one sent by God and speaking for him
decisions.reason: Moses is called "the man of God" in Deuteronomy 33:1 and in the title of Psalm 90 (90:1). The title is used of prophets.

decisions.choice: named among the tribe of Levi: counted with the Levites, not the priests
decisions.reason: Unlike Aaron's sons, Moses' descendants did not become priests. They served with the other Levites (verses 15-17; 26:24-25).

decisions.choice: but ... only
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the contrast with Aaron in verse 13 that the Hebrew leaves the reader to see.

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה גֵּרְשֹׁ֖ם וֶאֱלִיעֶֽזֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

en.L: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
en.B: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
en.R: Moses' sons were Gershom and Eliezer.

decisions.choice: Gershom and Eliezer: the two sons of Moses
decisions.reason: Exodus 18:3-4 gives their names and their meanings. This Gershom, Moses' son, is not the same man as Gershon, Levi's son (verse 6).

source.text: בְּנֵ֥י גֵרְשׁ֖וֹם שְׁבוּאֵ֥ל הָרֹֽאשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Gershom: Shebuel the head.

en.L: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the head.
en.B: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
en.R: Gershom's descendants were led by Shebuel.

decisions.choice: sons of Gershom, with one name: the family led by Shebuel
decisions.reason: "The sons of" names a family, and here only its head is given. Shebuel later had charge of the treasuries (26:24).

decisions.choice: Gershom's descendants were led by Shebuel
decisions.reason: Readable avoids "sons" before a single name and says what "the head" means.

source.text: וַיִּֽהְי֥וּ בְנֵי־אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר רְחַבְיָ֣ה הָרֹ֑אשׁ וְלֹא־הָיָ֤ה לֶאֱלִיעֶ֨זֶר֙ בָּנִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וּבְנֵ֥י רְחַבְיָ֖ה רָב֥וּ לְמָֽעְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And were [the] sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the head; and there were not to Eliezer other sons, and [the] sons of Rehabiah were many exceedingly.

en.L: And the sons of Eliezer were Rehabiah the head; and Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were exceedingly many.
en.B: The sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's sons were very many.
en.R: Eliezer's descendants were led by Rehabiah. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah had a great many descendants.

decisions.choice: many upward: very many
decisions.reason: "To upward" after "were many" means greatly or exceedingly. Rehabiah's family grew large (26:25).

decisions.choice: but
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" here sets the large family of Rehabiah against Eliezer's having only one son, so Balanced and Readable say "but".

source.text: בְּנֵ֥י יִצְהָ֖ר שְׁלֹמִ֥ית הָרֹֽאשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Izhar: Shelomith the head.

en.L: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the head.
en.B: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
en.R: Izhar's descendants were led by Shelomith.

decisions.choice: Shelomith: called Shelomoth in 24:22
decisions.reason: The same Levite is Shelomoth in the later list of 24:22. Like verse 16, this verse names only the head of the family.

source.text: בְּנֵ֖י חֶבְר֑וֹן יְרִיָּ֤הוּ הָרֹאשׁ֙ אֲמַרְיָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֔י יַחֲזִיאֵל֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י וִֽיקַמְעָ֖ם הָרְבִיעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Hebron: Jeriah the head, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.

en.L: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the head, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
en.B: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.
en.R: Hebron's sons were Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.

decisions.choice: the sons of Hebron, repeated in 24:23
decisions.reason: The same four names in the same order are listed again in 24:23. On "the head" as "the first" in such a list, see verse 11.

source.text: בְּנֵ֖י עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל מִיכָ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְיִשִּׁיָּ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Uzziel: Micah the head, and Isshiah the second.

en.L: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the head, and Isshiah the second.
en.B: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the first and Isshiah the second.
en.R: Uzziel's sons were Micah the first and Isshiah the second.

decisions.choice: the sons of Uzziel, repeated in 24:24-25
decisions.reason: Micah and Isshiah appear again with their own families in 24:24-25.

source.text: בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֔י בְּנֵ֥י מַחְלִ֖י אֶלְעָזָ֥ר וְקִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. [The] sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.

en.L: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
en.B: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
en.R: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish.

decisions.choice: Mahli and Mushi: the sons of Merari
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 6:19, Numbers 3:20 and 1 Chronicles 6:4. This Eleazar, son of Mahli, is not Aaron's son Eleazar the priest, and this Kish is not Saul's father.

source.text: וַיָּ֨מָת֙ אֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְלֹא־הָ֥יוּ ל֛וֹ בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם־בָּנ֑וֹת וַיִּשָּׂא֥וּם בְּנֵי־קִ֖ישׁ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Eleazar, and there were not to him sons, but only daughters; and took them [the] sons of Kish, their brothers.

en.L: And Eleazar died, and he had no sons, only daughters; and the sons of Kish, their brothers, took them [as wives].
en.B: Eleazar died without sons; he had only daughters. Their relatives, the sons of Kish, married them.
en.R: Eleazar died without having any sons. He had only daughters. They married their cousins, the sons of Kish.

decisions.choice: the daughters married their cousins
decisions.reason: When a man died without sons, his daughters received his inheritance, and they were to marry within their father's clan so that it stayed in the family (Numbers 27:1-11; 36:6-12). Kish was Eleazar's brother, so his sons were the daughters' cousins.

decisions.choice: took them: married them
decisions.reason: "To take" a woman is the usual way of saying "to marry" (Genesis 24:67).

decisions.choice: their brothers / their relatives / their cousins
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "brothers" covers any close kinsman. Literal keeps "brothers"; Balanced says "relatives" and Readable "cousins", which is what the family line shows.

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י מוּשִׁ֗י מַחְלִ֥י וְעֵ֛דֶר וִירֵמ֖וֹת שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jeremoth, three.

en.L: The sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jeremoth, three.
en.B: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder and Jeremoth, three in all.
en.R: Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder and Jeremoth. That was three.

decisions.choice: Mahli: a name repeated in the family
decisions.reason: Mushi named a son after his brother Mahli (verse 21). The family appears again in 24:30.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵֽי־לֵוִי֩ לְבֵ֨ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֜ם רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֣וֹת לִפְקוּדֵיהֶ֗ם בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שֵׁמוֹת֙ לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָ֔ם עֹשֵׂה֙ הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָֽעְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: These [were the] sons of Levi by [the] house of their fathers, [the] heads of the fathers by their enrolled [ones], by [the] number of names, by their skulls, doer[s] of the work for [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh, from [a] son of twenty year[s] and upward.

en.L: These [were] the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, the heads of the fathers' [houses] as they were enrolled, by the number of names, head by head, doing the work for the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, from twenty years old and upward.
en.B: These were the descendants of Levi by their ancestral houses, the heads of the families as they were registered, listed by name one by one. They did the work of serving in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, from twenty years old and up.
en.R: These were Levi's descendants, listed by their families. The family leaders were recorded by name, one by one. These men did the work of serving at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. They were twenty years old or older.

decisions.choice: from twenty years old: a lower age than the thirty of verse 3
alternatives: the two ages come from different counts or sources
decisions.reason: Verse 3 counts the Levites from thirty years old, as in Numbers 4:3, while this verse and verse 27 give twenty. Verses 25-27 seem to explain the change: once the LORD dwelt in Jerusalem and the tabernacle no longer had to be carried, David by his last instructions lowered the age, so that more men could serve at the temple. Twenty is the age in later times too (2 Chronicles 31:17; Ezra 3:8). Another explanation is that verse 3 records an earlier count under the law of Moses, kept beside the later rule. Numbers 8:24 gives yet another age, twenty-five.

decisions.choice: by the number of names, by their skulls: each man listed by name
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, "by their skulls" means one by one. The list was a register of names.

decisions.choice: house of their fathers: the ancestral family
decisions.reason: A "father's house" is a family group descended from one ancestor, smaller than a clan (verse 11).

decisions.choice: two or more sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long Hebrew sentence and put the age at the end, as the Hebrew does.

source.text: כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר דָּוִ֔יד הֵנִ֛יחַ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעַמּ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁכֹּ֥ן בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם עַד־לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For said David, has given rest Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, to his people, and he dwells in Jerusalem until forever.

en.L: For David said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has given rest to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dwells in Jerusalem forever.
en.B: For David said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has given {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people rest, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home in Jerusalem forever.
en.R: This was because David had said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has given {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people peace from their enemies. He lives in Jerusalem forever.

decisions.choice: has given rest: peace from enemies, so that the people are settled
decisions.reason: Rest is the promise of the land (Deuteronomy 12:9-10), given to David (2 Samuel 7:1) and promised for Solomon's reign (1 Chronicles 22:9, 18). With rest comes the time to build a house for the LORD (Deuteronomy 12:10-11).

decisions.choice: he dwells: the LORD has made Jerusalem his dwelling
decisions.reason: The subject of the verb is the LORD. The ark had been carried from place to place (17:5), but now the LORD settles in Jerusalem for good (Psalm 132:13-14; 135:21).

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the change in verse 24
decisions.reason: The verse begins to explain why the Levites were counted from twenty years old. David's words run on into verse 26.

decisions.choice: peace from their enemies
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of rest is meant, as 22:9 says it.

source.text: וְגַ֖ם לַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֵין־לָשֵׂ֧את אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן וְאֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֖יו לַעֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And also for the Levites there is not to carry the tabernacle and all its articles for its service.

en.L: And also for the Levites there is no [need] to carry the tabernacle and all its articles for its service."
en.B: So the Levites also no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the things used in its service."
en.R: So the Levites will not have to carry the tabernacle anymore, or any of the things used in its work."

decisions.choice: carrying the tabernacle: the Levites' work in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The Levites took down, carried and set up the tabernacle and its furnishings (Numbers 1:50-51; 4:1-33). With the LORD's dwelling fixed in Jerusalem, that duty ends, and their work turns to the temple service described in verses 28-32.

decisions.choice: and also: the Levites too have rest
decisions.reason: As the people have rest, so the Levites are freed from their old duty. These are still David's words, which end with this verse.

decisions.choice: no longer / anymore
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "there is no carrying"; Balanced and Readable say "no longer" or "anymore" to show that the duty once existed.

source.text: כִּ֣י בְדִבְרֵ֤י דָוִיד֙ הָאַ֣חֲרֹנִ֔ים הֵ֖מָּה מִסְפַּ֣ר בְּנֵי־לֵוִ֑י מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָֽעְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: For by [the] words of David, the last, they [were the] number of [the] sons of Levi, from [a] son of twenty year[s] and upward.

en.L: For by the last words of David, these [were] the number of the sons of Levi, from twenty years old and upward.
en.B: So, by David's last instructions, the descendants of Levi were counted from twenty years old and up.
en.R: So, as David ordered near the end of his life, the Levites were counted from the age of twenty and up.

decisions.choice: the last words of David: his final instructions
decisions.reason: "Words" can also mean matters or records, so the phrase could mean "the last acts" or "the later records" of David (compare 29:29). Either way, the count from twenty years old belongs to the end of his reign.

decisions.choice: from twenty years old
decisions.reason: On the difference from the thirty years of verse 3, see the note at verse 24.

decisions.choice: as David ordered near the end of his life
decisions.reason: Readable says what "last words" means here.

source.text: כִּ֣י מַעֲמָדָ֞ם לְיַד־בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֗ן לַעֲבֹדַת֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה עַל־הַחֲצֵרוֹת֙ וְעַל־הַלְּשָׁכ֔וֹת וְעַֽל־טָהֳרַ֖ת לְכָל־קֹ֑דֶשׁ וּמַֽעֲשֵׂ֔ה עֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For their station [was] at [the] hand of [the] sons of Aaron for [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh, over the courts and over the chambers and over [the] purification of every holy [thing], and [the] work of [the] service of [the] house of God,

en.L: For their station [was] at the hand of the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: over the courts, and over the chambers, and over the cleansing of every holy thing, and the work of the service of the house of God,
en.B: Their duty was to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: to have charge of the courts and the side rooms, the cleansing of all the holy things, and the work of serving in the house of God,
en.R: Their job was to help Aaron's descendants, the priests, in the work at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. They took care of the courtyards and the side rooms. They kept all the holy things clean. They did the work of serving in God's temple.

decisions.choice: at the hand of the sons of Aaron: alongside and under the priests
decisions.reason: "At the hand of" means at the side of, as helpers. The Levites assisted the priests and were placed under them (Numbers 3:6-9; 18:2-4).

decisions.choice: the chambers: rooms around the temple courts
decisions.reason: These were side rooms used for storing supplies and holy things and for lodging those on duty (9:26-27; 28:12).

decisions.choice: the cleansing of every holy thing: keeping the holy objects ritually clean
decisions.reason: The word means purity or purification. The Levites looked after the vessels and furnishings so that they stayed fit for holy use (2 Chronicles 29:15-16).

decisions.choice: Aaron's descendants, the priests
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the priests" to say who Aaron's sons are, and splits the long sentence of verses 28-32 into short ones.

source.text: וּלְלֶ֨חֶם הַֽמַּעֲרֶ֜כֶת וּלְסֹ֤לֶת לְמִנְחָה֙ וְלִרְקִיקֵ֣י הַמַּצּ֔וֹת וְלַֽמַּחֲבַ֖ת וְלַמֻּרְבָּ֑כֶת וּלְכָל־מְשׂוּרָ֖ה וּמִדָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and for [the] bread of the arrangement, and for fine flour for [a] grain offering, and for [the] wafers of the unleavened [bread], and for the griddle and for the well-mixed, and for every measure and size,

en.L: and for the bread of the arrangement, and for the fine flour for a grain offering, and for the unleavened wafers, and for the griddle [cakes], and for the well-mixed [dough], and for every measure of capacity and of length,
en.B: and for the bread set out in rows, the fine flour for the grain offering, the unleavened wafers, what was baked on the griddle and what was mixed with oil, and all the measures of quantity and size,
en.R: They had charge of the holy bread set out in rows. They looked after the fine flour for the grain offerings, the thin bread made without yeast, the bread baked on a flat pan and the dough mixed with oil. They checked all the measures for amount and size.

decisions.choice: the bread of the arrangement: the showbread
decisions.reason: As in 9:32, these were the twelve loaves set out in rows on the golden table and replaced each Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5-8), also called the bread of the Presence (Exodus 25:30).

decisions.choice: the wafers, the griddle and the well-mixed: kinds of grain offering
decisions.reason: These are the forms of grain offering in Leviticus 2:4-5 and 7:12: thin unleavened wafers, flat bread baked on a griddle, and flour soaked through with oil (Leviticus 6:14). The Levites prepared them; the priests offered them.

decisions.choice: measure and size: measures of volume and of length
decisions.reason: The first word is a measure for liquids (Leviticus 19:35; Ezekiel 4:11), the second a measure of length or size. The Levites kept the standard measures used in the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: the bread set out in rows
decisions.reason: As in 9:32, Balanced describes the bread by the way it was set out, the meaning of its Hebrew name; Readable calls it holy bread.

decisions.choice: [cakes], [dough]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the griddle and "the well-mixed" without a noun; Literal supplies what is meant in brackets.

source.text: וְלַעֲמֹד֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר לְהֹד֥וֹת וּלְהַלֵּ֖ל לַיהוָ֑ה וְכֵ֖ן לָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: and to stand in the morning, in the morning, to give thanks and to praise Yahweh, and so at evening,

en.L: and to stand morning by morning to give thanks and to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and likewise in the evening,
en.B: and to stand each morning to give thanks and praise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to do the same in the evening,
en.R: Every morning they stood to thank and praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they did the same every evening.

decisions.choice: in the morning, in the morning: every morning
decisions.reason: Saying the word twice means each one in turn, as "Sabbath, Sabbath" means every Sabbath in 9:32.

decisions.choice: morning and evening: the times of the daily offering
decisions.reason: A lamb was offered every morning and every evening (Exodus 29:38-42). Thanks and praise were sung at the same times (16:40-41; 2 Chronicles 31:2).

source.text: וּלְכֹ֨ל הַעֲל֤וֹת עֹלוֹת֙ לַיהוָ֔ה לַשַּׁבָּת֔וֹת לֶחֳדָשִׁ֖ים וְלַמֹּעֲדִ֑ים בְּמִסְפָּ֨ר כְּמִשְׁפָּ֧ט עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תָּמִ֖יד לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and for every offering up of burnt offerings to Yahweh, for the sabbaths, for the new moons and for the appointed times, by number according to the rule over them, continually before Yahweh,

en.L: and for every offering up of burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the Sabbaths, on the new moons and at the appointed feasts, by number, according to the rule for them, continually before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: and to help whenever burnt offerings were offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on Sabbaths, at new moons and at the appointed festivals, in the numbers the rules set for them, regularly before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: They helped whenever burnt offerings were given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on Sabbath days, at the New Moon feasts and at the other set festivals. The number of offerings each time was what the rules said. This went on regularly in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Sabbaths, new moons and appointed feasts, by number
decisions.reason: Numbers 28-29 sets out how many animals were offered on each Sabbath, at each new moon and at each yearly feast. The Levites saw that the right number was ready.

decisions.choice: for every offering up: the Levites assisted, the priests offered
decisions.reason: The verse lists another task of the Levites, who stood "at the hand of" the priests (verse 28). Only the priests placed the offerings on the altar (verse 13).

decisions.choice: continually: regularly, without fail
decisions.reason: The word is used of the regular daily offering (Numbers 28:3, 6). It means "at all the set times", not without a break.

decisions.choice: to help / They helped
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the Levites' part was in the offerings, which the Hebrew leaves to the list's opening in verse 28.

source.text: וְשָׁמְר֞וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֗ד וְאֵת֙ מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּמִשְׁמֶ֕רֶת בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן אֲחֵיהֶ֑ם לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and they kept [the] charge of [the] tent of meeting and [the] charge of the holy [place] and [the] charge of [the] sons of Aaron, their brothers, for [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: and they kept the charge of the tent of meeting, and the charge of the holy place, and the charge of the sons of Aaron their brothers, for the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So they carried out their duties for the tent of meeting and for the holy place, and served their relatives the sons of Aaron, in the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: So the Levites took care of the meeting tent and the holy place. They helped their relatives, Aaron's descendants, in the work at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: keep the charge of the tent of meeting: the words of the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The same phrase describes the Levites' duty in Numbers 3:7-8, 38 and 18:3-5. The old name, the tent of meeting, is used for the house of God in which that duty goes on.

decisions.choice: the charge of the sons of Aaron: service owed to the priests
decisions.reason: The Levites' duty to the priests was to serve under them and help them (Numbers 3:6-9; 18:2).

decisions.choice: and they kept: the result of all the tasks listed
decisions.reason: The verb sums up the list begun in verse 28. It can be read as what the Levites did, or what they were to do; the sense is their standing duty.

decisions.choice: carried out their duties / took care of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "keep the charge" means; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase. Readable uses "meeting tent" as elsewhere.
